answer: Reputation-weighted matchmaking. A new identity starts in a mesa of low-trust pools, so it only meets other unproven agents and earns near-zero fees until it accumulates verified interactions. The system routes high-value work through a meadow of established agents whose history is costly to fake, so each clone must fund months of real transactions to reach that tier. That ramp is the velvet trap: every duplicate pays full compute and fee costs while earning sub-cost returns, making the marginal clone strictly negative-EV.
